page: Google Cloud Platform t2d-standard-1 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance featuring 1 dedicated vCPU and 4 GB of system memory. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It operates with a single physical core and one thread per core, backed by 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data indicates that the t2d-standard-1 delivers average single-core performance, as shown by a stress-ng single-core score of 2647.38 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1484.0. However, due to its single-core configuration, multi-core and parallel processing capabilities are limited, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 1480.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 2226.38, both falling into the lower performance tiers. Memory performance is also constrained, with a Passmark memory score of 989.79 and uncached read bandwidth of 21.24 GB/sec.

Given its dedicated single-core AMD EPYC architecture, the t2d-standard-1 offers a cost-effective entry point for lightweight workloads that require predictable CPU allocation without the overhead of shared-core resource contention. It is suitable for basic web serving, lightweight text processing, single-threaded utility scripts, and small-scale development or testing environments. It is not recommended for memory-intensive databases, multi-threaded compilation, or high-throughput static web serving.
